checks.command: swift package clean && swift test --filter EvidenceStore
checks.result: passed against Apple SDK SQLite; 8 tests, 0 failures, no deployment-target linker warning

acceptance_evidence.reference: The actor-owned WAL connection preserved 200 concurrent committed writes while 50 reads/integrity checks interleaved. Invalid multi-row insertion rolled back fully and a reopened store retained only committed evidence. Retention aggregated raw events into hourly summaries while preserving an unreviewed anomaly; a 12,000-row oversized fixture forced eviction plus VACUUM below the 10 MiB ceiling. SQLite backup produced a separately readable, integrity-ok database with matching event and snapshot counts. Corruption is rejected at open.

discovered_risks: The system-library module deliberately links Apple SDK libsqlite3 rather than a Homebrew build so the macOS 13 deployment target remains valid.
Hard size-ceiling enforcement may evict the oldest unreviewed anomaly only after normal age-based compaction is insufficient; forced eviction count is surfaced in RetentionReport.
Direct database access remains internal to the app-owned core; MCP must consume a later sanitized service boundary.

evidence: All changed paths are within Package.swift, Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/**, and Tests/DiskStewardCoreTests/EvidenceStore/**.
A clean database migrates transactionally to user_version=1, enables WAL/busy timeout/foreign keys, and returns PRAGMA quick_check=ok; newer schemas and corrupt files fail closed.
The Swift actor serializes one FULLMUTEX SQLite connection; the test interleaves 200 writes with 50 reads/integrity checks and retains exactly 200 events.
Batch validation failure after an earlier insert triggers ROLLBACK; close/reopen retains the prior committed event and excludes the partial batch.

Age-based retention aggregates eligible raw rows to hourly and hourly to daily summaries, bounds daily history, preserves unreviewed anomalies when possible, checkpoints WAL, and vacuums. A forced 12,000-row fixture contracts below 10 MiB.
SQLite's online backup API creates a consistent separate database; reopening reports 25 events, one snapshot, schema version 1, and integrity ok.

The event record accepts typed metadata fields only—no arbitrary payload, environment, command secret, or file-content field exists. Snapshot blobs encode the closed capacity-only StorageSnapshot contract.
Focused suite passed 8 tests, full suite passed 27 tests, build and diff checks passed, and clean linkage uses SDK libsqlite3 without the earlier Homebrew deployment warning.
